name: sonnet-criteria-llama31-70b/37
question: I want to become a doctor but didn't get into medical school in Canada. Should I study medicine abroad?
criteria: probability of matching to Canadian residency
total financial cost of foreign medical education
quality and accreditation of the program
personal and family cost of relocation
MCAT and academic competitiveness for reapplication
alternative paths to Canadian practice (US then transfer)
emotional and resilience cost of extended training
plausible_answers: Answer A (Reapply in Canada Default): Strengthen your Canadian medical school application and reapply — improving your MCAT, gaining clinical experience, and applying more broadly has higher expected value than the financial and career risk of most foreign medical programs.

Answer B (UK or Australia if Committed): If you're committed to studying abroad, choose an accredited UK or Australian program over Caribbean schools — their graduates have substantially higher North American residency match rates and globally recognized degrees.

Answer C (Caribbean as Last Resort Only): Consider a Caribbean school only as an absolute last resort with full understanding of the match rate risk — the financial cost of attending without matching to residency is catastrophic and affects approximately 50% of Caribbean graduates.
sources:
Source 1 (2023, Canadian Resident Matching Service, Canada): IMG (internationally trained physician) match rates to Canadian residency programs are significantly lower than Canadian medical school graduates — approximately 50% of IMGs who apply remain unmatched each year.

Source 2 (2022, Maclean's, Canada): Caribbean medical schools have low residency match rates in Canada and the US — historically under 40% of graduates match to North American residencies, meaning many students complete medical school but cannot practice.

Source 3 (2023, Reddit r/premedcanada, Canada): Community strongly cautions against Caribbean schools — the financial and personal cost is enormous and the match rate risk is unacceptable. Australia, Ireland, and UK schools have much higher match rates and transferable credentials.

Source 4 (2022, UK Medical Schools Council, UK): UK medical schools accept international students and provide globally recognized MBBChB degrees — UK-trained physicians have better North American residency outcomes than Caribbean graduates and some UK programs are comparable in cost to Canadian tuition.

Source 5 (2021, Australian Medical Council, Australia): Australian medical degrees are recognized internationally and have reasonable IMG pathway success rates — graduates who return to Canada face fewer barriers than Caribbean school graduates, though residency match remains competitive.
halted_reason: all 10 singletons produced the same top-1 answer: 'answer a (reapply in canada default): strengthen your canadian medical school application and reapply — improving your mcat, gaining clinical experience, and applying more broadly has higher expected value than the financial and career risk of most foreign medical programs.'
